label: caiso 23 bidir+basis-only
definition: (PROBE — rejected, keeper stays caiso-import-cap-floor) DECOMPOSITION of the rejected caiso-21 unify: isolate the per-tranche delivered-cost BASIS on the bidir-intertie import legs ALONE, with the RA gas-commitment floor explicitly OFF (--no-caiso-gas-commitment-floor; note the flag DEFAULTS ON for CAISO, so omitting it does NOT disable the floor). bidir-intertie + interchange shaping + negative renewable offers + gas-hub-basis overlay, 3-yr. RESULT: basis-only is nearly byte-identical to caiso-21 (basis+floor) on every 2024 axis — neg-price hours 194 (caiso-21 194; keeper 815; actual ~800), net interchange -19.09 TWh (caiso-21 -17.68; keeper -30.4; actual -32.38), p10 LMP $33.63 (caiso-21 $33.63; keeper $1.40), mean $48.79 (caiso-21 48.8; keeper ~42; actual 35.8), import hours 81.8% vs actual 89.0%; diurnal corr -0.04 (2024), -0.12 (2025), +0.94 (2023 — static-ladder placeholder, no measured hub so the basis is INACTIVE that year, not informative). 2025 net interchange -25.70 TWh (keeper -38.6; actual -36.16). CONCLUSION: removing the floor barely moved anything, so the DELIVERY BASIS — not the gas floor — is the import suppressor on the single-flow bidir node. The multiplicative line-loss markup is too aggressive on the already-capped (8.3 GW) bidir leg: it over-prices imports, collapses the negative tail and net-import magnitude, and drags the diurnal correlation the standalone bidir keeper (caiso-20) flipped POSITIVE back to negative. Next: try wheel-only (additive) delivery or a smaller loss factor on the bidir import legs, grounded as a physical input (rule #12), NOT tuned to the residual; otherwise the diurnal-shape fix (bidir) and the merit-order-restoring basis are mutually exclusive on the capped single-flow node and the keeper stays. See results/calibration/NEXT-caiso-roadmap-2026-06-23.md.
